Zobo Shooter

Use your strongest eligible Tatari quality, pick an arena you can enter, and understand the chance behind each attack.

Every attack is a chance

Zobos enter the arena and leave after a time. Each paid attack consumes coins according to the arena multiplier. Defeating a Zobo earns points; team score unlocks milestones.

Your team shares points. According to the published rules, item drops from your own kills are not shared.

Choose your Tatari and arena

  1. Use the highest eligible Tatari quality. The standard chance multiplier rises from 1.00 for Blue to 1.10 for Rainbow.
  2. Check the arena’s unlock requirement and your current coin balance. These are separate gates.
Higher quality improves chance proportionally. A 4.15% base chance becomes 4.565% with Rainbow, not 14.15%.

Power-ups

Defeating Zobos can drop Lock On and Enrage. Drops from your own kills belong to you; they are not shared with teammates.

Collect power-ups in the ×1 arena. Its lower cost gives you more attacks from the same coin budget, creating more opportunities to defeat Zobos and collect power-ups. Save them for higher-multiplier arenas. This gives more attempts, not a higher drop chance per kill.
Lock On

Auto-target Zobos through obstacles.

Enrage

Increase your attack speed.

Compare a boss attack

Points, cost, and risk

For the same target, a higher arena multiplier increases points and cost together. It does not by itself improve expected points per coin. Later arenas add different bosses, so the target pool still matters.

Set a budget, not an imaginary guarantee

Leaving after a spending limit can protect your budget. There is no verified rule that spending a fixed number of coins resets the next kill chance or makes a boss “due.” Another player can also finish a target while you are attacking.
